He assumed full control of the county around 1160 after reaching adulthood. His reign was marked by efforts to strengthen Tripoli's defenses against Muslim incursions. He reinforced the city walls and upgraded the citadel. Raymond sought alliances with neighboring Crusader states especially the Kingdom of Jerusalem. He participated in the campaign that followed the failed Second Crusade aiming to protect Christian holdings. In 1164 he joined a combined force that attacked Muslim positions in Syria. The expedition achieved limited success but demonstrated his commitment to the Crusader cause. Raymond also engaged in diplomacy with the Byzantine Empire hoping to secure naval support. He negotiated treaties that allowed trade goods to move through Tripoli's port. His diplomatic skill helped maintain a fragile peace during periods of tension. However his relationship with Jerusalem sometimes soured over disputes about territory and tribute. Despite these tensions he remained a key figure in the politics of the Outremer. His leadership contributed to the stability of Tripoli during a turbulent era.
